method: FX contract: alpha = classes of the categorical soft-label master (tone-group version, label-exact centres), identical for every CLUT with the same transparent entries; RGB free of class thresholds = continuous index field t (normalised convolution of the native index inside the opaque silhouette, sigma 0.55 texel: low frequencies locked to native) + band-limited turbulence (0.35 index steps) when the CLUT is a luminance ramp (Spearman >= 0.85), else categorical soft labels; glow break (new in v2): where two adjacent native indices are joined by a palette path that leaves the straight colour segment between them by more than 48 RGB under any rendered CLUT (an off-ramp entry, e.g. the grey-brown index 0 next to the red ramp on AFCCB3B5), the render uses the crisp categorical labels instead of the continuous index (soft weight over about half a texel), so no false bright halo appears between unrelated tones; per 32x32-texel cell light-energy gate vs native, applied as a smooth gain field (new in v2: per-cell log-gains bilinear between cell centres, 4 iterations, gains clamped 0.5..2; cells that are all black natively are zeroed hard because their light is only leakage), so no straight brightness step appears at cell borders inside a sprite. No material layer and no generated detail in this revision. v3: on B305DC32 the row of small spiky sprites (texel rect 0,232,256,16) is rendered from the categorical soft labels (crisp silhouettes, 1-texel line strokes) instead of the continuous index (soft blend over 0.35 texel at the rect edge); soft.strokes is on for both pages (it only changes label-rendered areas).
render_formula: t = smoothed native index (+ turbulence); rgb = lerp(P[floor t], P[ceil t]) inside the opaque silhouette, blended with the categorical label render by the glow-break weight (master/<TEX>-glowweight16-u8.npy); class = class(P[l_0]) of the soft-label master; smooth per-cell energy gain field; class stamped at every texel centre

class_validation.convention: class at pixel floor((i+0.5)*scale) of every native texel == class(CLUT[native index]); class 0 = raw 0x0000, 255 = STP, 127 = opaque

alpha_channel: categorical PSX classes (0 = raw 0x0000, 127 opaque, 255 STP), NOT opacity; exact at every native texel centre

glow.used: glow with break weight (labels where the index path leaves the colour segment); categorical labels inside label_rects
glow with break weight (labels where the index path leaves the colour segment)

honest_read: B305DC32 small spiky mine/star sprites (texel rows 232-247) now render from crisp categorical labels: silhouettes and 1-texel spikes read clearly, close to the native shapes, where v2 had soft blobs. Inside each sprite the grey tones posterise into rounded patches: a smoothed pixel-art look, not a photographic one.

Motion SIMULATION (review/motion-sim-v2-v3.*): the crisp sprites twinkle more than v2: 0.026 vs 0.012 at 9 px/texel and 0.117 vs 0.028 at 3 px/texel (native nearest 0.129 / 0.230). If these sprites are mostly seen small on screen, the soft v2 is the steadier choice; decide when AQ-03 shows their on-screen size.

Smoke, flames and the AFCCB3B5 page are unchanged from v2 (smoke control twinkle identical: 0.0015 / 0.0052). Strokes are on for both pages but only change label-rendered areas (the sprite row and the AFCCB3B5 glow-break regions).

AFCCB3B5: index 0 (grey-brown) is off the red ramp. In the first v2 build the continuous index drew a bright pink halo wherever index 0 met the dark reds. The glow-break weight now renders those 2738 texels with crisp categorical labels, and the halo is gone.

The light-energy gate is a smooth gain field (gains 1.0..1.48). Every cell lands within 3 % of native mean light, and no straight brightness step remains at the 32-texel cell borders. The old scalar gate left 7-18 % steps there. Two cells that are all black natively are zeroed: their light was only leakage from neighbours.
No generated detail: the planned FX v2 SDXL img2img pass for these pages has not run.
